samples.text:
The diagram shows the life cycle of the Atlantic salmon. There are seven stages and it is a cycle, because the adult salmon come back to the river where they was born.

Firstly, the eggs are laid in the gravel of the upper river and they hatch in spring. Then the baby fish are called alevin. They stay in the gravel and they feed on their yolk sac. After that, they become fry and they come out from the gravel to feed in the river.

Next stage is parr. The parr live in the river for 1–3 years. Then they become smolt, they turn silver and swim downstream to the sea. In the sea, the adult salmon feed and grow for 1–4 years, so they spend quite a long time there.

Finally, the salmon swim back up the same river to spawn, so the new eggs are laid and the cycle start again. Overall, the salmon spend some years in the river and some years in the sea, and in the end they return to the place where the cycle begin.
samples.why: Overview present but placed at the end · all seven stages and timings covered accurately · repetitive linking · simple vocabulary with some informality · several agreement and article errors that do not block meaning.

samples.text:
The diagram illustrates the life cycle of the Atlantic salmon, which is spent partly in a river and partly in the ocean.

Overall, the cycle consists of seven stages. The first four take place in the river, after which the fish migrate to the sea to mature before returning to the same river to spawn, so that the cycle begins again.

The eggs are laid in the gravel of the upper river and hatch in spring. The young fish, known as alevin, remain in the gravel at first and feed on their yolk sac. They then emerge as fry to feed in the river, and later develop into parr, which live in the river for between one and three years.

At the smolt stage, the fish turn silver and migrate downstream to the sea. As adults, they feed and grow in the ocean during 1–4 years. Finally, they make a return migration, swimming back up the same river in which they hatched in order to spawn, and new eggs are laid in the gravel of the upper river, which starts the whole cycle once again.
samples.why: Clear overview contrasting river and ocean phases · logical progression with varied cohesive devices · good topic vocabulary (spawn, migrate, emerge) · frequent error-free sentences with one preposition slip.

samples.text:
The diagram traces the life cycle of the Atlantic salmon across seven stages, from eggs laid in a river to mature adults returning to breed.

What stands out is that the fish spends its early life in fresh water and its adult life at sea, before a return migration to the river where it began brings the cycle full circle.

The cycle begins in the gravel of the upper river, where eggs are laid and hatch in spring. The newly hatched alevin remain in the gravel, sustained by their yolk sac, until they emerge as fry to feed in the river itself. They then develop into parr, a stage that lasts anywhere from one to three years.

Subsequently, the young salmon undergo a transformation into smolt, turning silver and migrating downstream to the sea. They spend the next 1–4 years in the ocean, feeding and growing, before undertaking the return migration, swimming back up the very river in which they began life in order to spawn. The eggs they lay mark the start of a new generation, and so the cycle repeats.
samples.why: Perceptive overview contrasting the freshwater and marine phases · stages and durations selected accurately · seamless cohesion · precise vocabulary (sustained by, undertaking) · wide range of structures · error-free.
